name: cloudflare
summary: Put the store's rate limits, geo blocks, custom rules and managed rulesets on its Cloudflare zone.

env.name: CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID
env.comment: The zone's ID (Cloudflare dashboard, the domain's Overview page, API section)

env.name: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
env.comment: An API token scoped to that zone only, with Zone › Zone › Read, Zone › Zone WAF › Edit and Zone › Cache Rules › Edit

next: Create the API token in the Cloudflare dashboard (My Profile, API Tokens) with three permissions on this zone only: Zone › Zone › Read, Zone › Zone WAF › Edit and Zone › Cache Rules › Edit.

Behind Cloudflare every request reaches the API from an edge address, so the in-process rate limiter would key on the edge: list the proxy that connects to the API in NYMBAL_TRUSTED_PROXIES (Cloudflare's published ranges when it reaches the API directly, uniquelocal when your platform's proxy sits behind Cloudflare), and set NYMBAL_CLIENT_IP_HEADER=CF-Connecting-IP so the API reads the client from Cloudflare's header. Use the header only when every request to that proxy passes through Cloudflare: otherwise a client that reaches the origin directly can set it.

The zone's plan limits security.rateLimit: the Free plan allows one rate limit with a 10s window, Pro two with 10s or 1m (the scaffold's four fit Business and up). A throttle action needs the Enterprise plan: on Free, Pro or Business change the scaffold's two throttle entries (/api/*, /webhooks/*) to block or challenge. nymbal security:plan names each limit the plan refuses.
Run nymbal security:plan to see the rules, then nymbal security:apply to put them on the zone; nymbal security:drift reports a dashboard edit.
